chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabi said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was asked about a man who advanced dirhams for five measures of wheat or barley for a specified term, and the one who owed the wheat or barley was unable to take all of what was due to him when it became due, so he asked the creditor to take half or a third or less or more of the food, and take the principal of what remained of the food in dirhams. He said, 'There is no harm.'

And regarding saffron, a man advances dirhams for twenty mithqals or less or more. He said, 'There is no harm if the one who owes the saffron is unable to give him all his due, so he takes half his right or a third or two-thirds, and takes the principal of what remains of his right.'

key_terms.إِسْلَام: Advancing payment or giving in trust

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to settle a debt of goods by taking part of the goods and the rest in cash?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the mechanism of *salam* settlement when the debtor lacks the full commodity, permitting the creditor to accept a partial physical delivery and convert the remainder into cash. Imam al-Sadiq’s ruling of 'la ba'sa' (no objection) establishes flexibility in debt resolution, ensuring creditors are not disadvantaged by the debtor's temporary inability to provide the full kind, a principle vital for commercial stability in Shia jurisprudence. It highlights the distinction between the obligation of the specific commodity and the monetary value attached to the unpaid portion.
